notation: A field type is string | number | boolean | object | array | any; a trailing ? marks it optional.

transport.health: GET /health — no auth; answers { ok, farm: { id, name }, contract }
transport.pair: POST /pair — body is a pair.request, answer is a pair.response or { error }
transport.socket: GET /ws — WebSocket upgrade; every message is one JSON frame with a `kind`
transport.view: GET /view/<page>?view=<view id> — the page's HTML as the remote host renders it, the same page code as in VS Code with afRemote.js in place of acquireVsCodeApi; header Authorization: AF <welcome.session>
transport.res: GET /res/<path> — the resources a page loads (media/*.js, common.css, fonts, images); header Authorization: AF <welcome.session>; anything outside the page resource folders is 404
transport.tls: The host serves its own certificate; the client pins the SHA-256 fingerprint it read from the pairing URI and never trusts any other.
transport.signature: ECDSA P-256 with SHA-256 (DER), over the UTF-8 text `agentfarm.remote/1|<farm id>|<device id>|<nonce>`; the device public key is X.509 SubjectPublicKeyInfo DER, base64.
transport.discovery: While the host listens on the local network it answers mDNS (DNS-SD) for _agentfarm._tcp.local: SRV gives its port, A its private IPv4 addresses, TXT farm=<farm id> and contract=<version>. A paired client that finds its farm's id there tries that address too; pairing and the pinned certificate are unchanged.

spoken.text: developer soruyor: Hangisi? Seçenekler: A, B.
developer's question answers itself in 2 minutes.
developer wants to run: git status.
Weekly cut asks: Ship it? Options: Yes, No.

rules: The host speaks first on /ws with a challenge; the client answers hello; nothing else is accepted before welcome.
A client ignores an event type it does not know; a host refuses a frame kind it does not know with result ok:false (for call) or by dropping it (otherwise).
Every call carries an id the client generated. A host that has already answered that id answers again with the stored result and duplicate:true, and never runs the op twice.
Event seq numbers only grow. hello.resumeAfter asks for every event after that seq; when they are no longer kept the host sends one gap frame, then the rest.
A contract version the other side does not speak ends the socket with refuse reason contract, naming the version it needs.
Secrets never travel: no frame carries a secret value, only whether one exists.

An alerting event (ask.opened, ask.answersSoon, permission.opened, turn.finished, notice.posted, quota.warn, gate.opened, mission.ended) the farm's alert gate silences right now carries quiet { reasons: [fleet | session | quiet-hours], detail }: the farm would not ring for it, and the reasons say which rule; a client that follows the farm's alert rules shows it without ringing. An event without quiet is one the farm would ring for.

While VS Code is closed the farm's headless service may hold the socket (same farm id, certificate and devices): it sends no events and serves no pages, and answers every call ok:false with one sentence except farm.ping, farm.away (away:true, since, the last snapshot and its age) and farm.open (scope manage: starts VS Code; the socket then closes and the client reconnects to the full farm). A running farm answers farm.away with away:false.

A client that can be woken registers its FCM registration token with call remote.wake.register { token } (any scope, its own device only; an empty token clears it; revoking the device drops it; the headless service takes it too). When an alerting event without quiet comes and that device has no socket open, the farm sends it an FCM data message { wake: "1", farm: <farm id> } (android priority high, collapse key agentfarm-wake), throttled per device; nothing of the event goes through Google — the client connects and reads what it missed with hello.resumeAfter. welcome.features["remote.wake"] says whether this farm can send wakes at all (it needs a Firebase service account key in its Secrets), with the reason when it cannot.

permission.opened.key is the Needs You row key (needKey): a client answers with call needs.act { key, action: permission-allow | permission-deny } and never builds the key itself; console.answer answers questions only.

gate.opened is a workflow supervisor waiting on a person: a client answers it with call workflows.answer { id: gateId, option (1-based) | answer } (scope answer); the first answer anywhere wins, and gate.closed then takes it off every client. A window reload drops an open gate without gate.closed: workflows.answer then answers ok:false, and the client lets the alert go. mission.ended says a top-level mission run ended, outcome done or failed.

welcome.wake lists the farm's network cards on the local network as { mac, broadcast }, absent off the LAN. A client that keeps it may wake the sleeping PC with a Wake-on-LAN magic packet (six 0xFF bytes, then the MAC sixteen times) sent by UDP to port 9 of broadcast, then connect again.
welcome.session authorizes /view and /res for that device only while its socket is open; the host forgets it when the socket closes, and a client never stores it.

spoken { text, lang } is what the host's own reader says for the event: text already cleaned for a voice and cut to the event's length, lang the BCP-47 primary tag of the language it is in. A client that reads aloud reads it as is and picks a voice for lang; it is absent when there is nothing to say, and a client falls back to its own reading then.

watch asks the host to push one Console session's changes as live frames. Depth full carries agent, status, turnSince, cost, steerable, step (the call in flight, null between calls), asking (as console.sessions says it) and, in messages, the rows new or changed since the last frame, in sessions.read's words (key, turn, role, ts, text?, tool?, input?, isError?, clipped?). Depth summary carries the same without messages, at most once a second per session; session "*" with depth summary watches every Console session. A live frame is not numbered and never replayed: after a reconnect the client watches again and reads what it missed with sessions.read, and a live row is provisional until the transcript read by sessions.read carries it. The host ends a watch with unwatch (reason ended when the session goes, unavailable when it cannot be watched); a socket's watches end with it.

ops names the bridge ops a client draws its own screens from and the fields of their answers it reads: answer (array or object), fields (an object answer's own), list (the field of an object answer that holds its rows) and row (each row's). A host may answer more than is declared; it never answers less or renames a field. console.sessions with view summary answers exactly the declared row fields. sessions.recent with view page answers { rows, next }: the sessions it selects, newest activity first, after cursor (a cursor names a row: its activity time and id, so a page never shifts when a session appears on top); next is the cursor of the following page and null on the last; limit is at most 50, 20 by default. A page row's lastLine is the first line of the last thing the agent said, absent when it was not read; status is what a Console card or the live monitor says the session is doing, null when neither knows it.
